newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM SEEKS CZK 5 BLN IN FLOOD RELIEF BONDS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM SEEKS CZK 5 BLN IN FLOOD RELIEF BONDS.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday the government would ask parliament to approve issues totalling up to five billion crowns in domestic government bonds to raise emergency funds for flood relief in the eastern part of the country.

"We have to ask the parliament for an approval of this credit. We intend to ask the parliament today or tomorrow (approval) of an expense of up to five billion crowns," Klaus told a news conference after an extraordinary cabinet meeting on the floods.
He said the bonds what be intended to be issued to private individuals and institions and would have denominations ranging from 500 crowns to one million crowns.
He added that the maturity had not been decided.
Klaus said he expected parliament to consider the plan quickly in extraordinary procedings, and said it should be approved "without problems".

Klaus also said the government would ask parliament to transfer three billion crowns in proceeds from the privatisation of smaller businesses completed earlier this decade for the floor relief effort.
The cabinet on Wednesday approved just over one billion crowns from various sources at its disposal for emergency relief in the floods which began last weekend and have become the worst the century.
Damage to buildings, homes, and infrastructure is expected to be in the tens of billions of crowns.
